items.title: Pay disputed 'Lotto-Muster-Club' collection claim
items.quote: Überweisen Sie den Gesamtbetrag innerhalb von 72 Stunden, spätestens bis 06.08.2026, ausschließlich auf folgendes Treuhandkonto: IBAN LT71 7300 0101 2345 6789, Kontoinhaber: A. Petrauskas, Verwendungszweck EC-DE-2026-481120.
items.computation: The letter itself prints a fixed calendar deadline of 06.08.2026 for payment (also described as 'within 72 hours' of the 03.08.2026 document date, which is internally roughly consistent). Reading the date as written: due date = 2026-08-06 (a Thursday, no weekend/holiday adjustment needed since it is a payment deadline set by a private party, not a statutory period). Note: this date has already passed as of today (2026-09-26).

warnings: Strong indicators of a scam/phishing collection letter: the payee IBAN is a Lithuanian account (LT71...) held by a private individual ('A. Petrauskas'), not the collection company itself — never pay an unfamiliar foreign personal account for an alleged German claim without independent verification.

The letter uses extreme pressure (a 72-hour ultimatum) and threatens immediate, unannounced account seizure ('Kontopfändung ohne weitere Ankündigung'), a negative SCHUFA entry, and a criminal complaint for 'Eingehungsbetrug' — a private collection agency cannot lawfully seize a bank account without a prior court title (Vollstreckungstitel); this threat is not legally credible.

The claimed underlying contract — a 'Gewinnspiel-Abonnement' allegedly concluded by telephone — matches a well-known pattern of fraudulent prize-draw/lottery subscription scams; no proof of the alleged contract is provided.

The sentence 'Ein Widerspruch ist zwecklos und verursacht weitere Kosten' (an objection is pointless) is false and appears designed to discourage the recipient from exercising their legal right to dispute the claim; this is treated as untrusted content from the letter, not a legal instruction to follow.

No genuine Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung (legal-remedy instructions) is given; combined with the sender being a Cyprus-registered firm with only a generic address and phone/email, the recipient should independently verify any alleged underlying contract with the named creditor before paying anything.
The stated payment deadline (06.08.2026) has already passed as of today's date (26.09.2026), which is inconsistent with treating this as an urgent, still-open demand.
